headline: Quantum Limits in Correlation, Capacity, and Dynamics
summary: Today's papers explore the foundational boundaries separating quantum from classical systems across multiple fronts. Theoretical results pin down the exact criteria governing non-local correlations and non-classical dynamics, while operational studies establish rigorous limits on quantum tomography, superactivation of private capacity, and monitored transport.

themes.title: Foundations of Quantum Correlations
themes.body: Studies establish rigorous bounds distinguishing quantum correlations from classical and general post-quantum behaviors via information causality and distinct vacuum fluctuation signatures.

themes.title: Quantum Information and Operational Limits
themes.body: Works quantify fundamental operational constraints in quantum networks and tomography, uncovering superactivation of zero-private-capacity channels and tight bounds for bounded-sample measurements.

themes.title: Thermodynamics and Open Dynamics
themes.body: Investigations into physical dynamics reveal how Noether symmetries govern deterministic energy harvesting and how monitoring drives return phase transitions in long-range walks.

connections.body: Both papers interrogate what fundamentally separates classical from quantum physics beyond traditional Bell-type inequalities, using information-theoretic principles and Hamiltonian evolution footprints respectively.
